html:
Pather Panchali is a 1955 Bengali film, the first that Satyajit Ray directed. It adapts the 1929 novel by Bibhutibhushan Bandyopadhyay about a poor Brahmin family in a village in Bengal, seen through the eyes of the boy Apu and his sister Durga.

Ray had no film training and shot it over several years with an amateur cast, a small crew and money that kept running out; the government of West Bengal stepped in to finish it. The music was by Ravi Shankar.

It won a prize at the 1956 Cannes festival and showed the world an Indian cinema far from the song and dance films of Bombay. Ray went on to make two sequels, which together form The Apu Trilogy. Critics still list it among the best films ever made, and it set the path for India's art cinema in the decades after independence.
